extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, assignees, applicants, and USPTO personnel
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and regulatory requirements for an assignee or owner to establish the right to request or take action in U.S. patent matters (pre- and post-September 16, 2012 rules). Covers who may act, what evidence is required, signature authority, timing, continuing applications, and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who owns the national patent application
rubrics_metrics.description: A national patent application is owned by one of the following individual or composite entities: (A) the inventor(s); (B) an assignee or multiple assignees of the inventor(s); or (C) some combination of the assignee(s), and inventor(s) who have not assigned away their right, title and interest in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-AIA 37 CFR 3.71(b)(1) and (2) identify the owner/assignee that can take action in patent matters. When multiple owners exist they must act together as a composite entity to conduct prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single (individual) assignee may act alone
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is a single assignee of the entire right, title and interest in the patent application, the single assignee may act alone to conduct the prosecution of an application or other patent proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is subject to compliance with the applicable submission requirements (pre-AIA 37 CFR 3.73(b) or 37 CFR 3.73(c)) and being made of record (e.g., by filing the required statement and, where applicable, a request to change the applicant under 37 CFR 1.46).

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial assignees and retained-inventor ownership rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Where at least one inventor retains an ownership interest together with partial assignee(s), the combination of all partial assignees and inventors retaining ownership interest is needed to conduct prosecution of an application (unless certain petitions have been granted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'partial assignee' is any assignee of record who has less than the entire right, title and interest in the application. Exception: if an inventor refused to join and a petition under 37 CFR 1.47 (pre-AIA) or 1.46(b)(2) (post-AIA) has been granted, different rules may apply. In reissue or inventorship-correction contexts, non-assigned inventors must consent to reissue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing ownership — documentary evidence required
rubrics_metrics.description: Ownership is established by submitting a signed statement identifying the assignee accompanied by either (A) documentary evidence of a chain of title from the original owner to the assignee (e.g., copy of an executed assignment) with a statement that it was or is being submitted for recordation under 37 CFR 3.11, or (B) a statement specifying where such evidence is recorded (e.g., reel and frame number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents submitted to establish ownership are required to be recorded or submitted for recordation pursuant to 37 CFR 3.11 as a condition to permitting the assignee to take action. 35 U.S.C. 261 requires transfer of ownership by assignment to be in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of ownership submission
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission establishing ownership must be submitted prior to, or at the same time as, the paper requesting or taking action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the ownership submission is not present when the action is submitted, the action sought will not be given effect. If the submission is later filed, that later date becomes the date of the request for action or the date of the assignee’s action taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may sign the ownership submission
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission establishing ownership must be signed by a party authorized to act on behalf of the assignee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted signatories include: (A) a person in the organization having apparent authority (officers such as CEO, president, vice-president, secretary, treasurer are presumed to have authority); (B) any person if the submission states that the person signing is authorized to act on behalf of the assignee; (C) a person empowered by an organizational resolution if a copy of the resolution is or was previously submitted; and (post-AIA) (D) a patent practitioner of record. A power of attorney to a practitioner does not alone make that practitioner an officer or empower them to sign absent other authority. For titles that do not clearly indicate officer status, the submission should indicate the signer's authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple partial assignees — extent of interest must be set forth
rubrics_metrics.description: When more than one assignee holds the right, title and interest, each partial assignee must provide a submission under 37 CFR 3.73(c) and in each submission the extent of each assignee’s interest must be set forth so the Office can determine whether the entire right, title and interest holders have been obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If extent of ownership is not set forth, the Office may refuse to accept the submission as an establishment of ownership. Options include specifying percentages for each owner (37 CFR 3.73(c)(2)(i)) or identifying the parties (including inventors) who together own the entire interest and stating that they collectively own it (37 CFR 3.73(c)(2)(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicting 37 CFR 3.73 statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where two or more conflicting 37 CFR 3.73 statements exist in an application or proceeding, the statement with the latest date of submission will normally control as to establishment of the assignee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the ownership established as controlling is contested on the record by another party who submitted a conflicting statement, the matter is forwarded to the Office of Patent Legal Administration (or the Director) to resolve procedural issues and determine which purported assignee will control prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Becoming of record and change of applicant requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignee who is not the original applicant must become the applicant under 37 CFR 1.46 in order to request or take action in a patent application; a request to change the applicant under 37 CFR 1.46(c)(2) must be filed and accompanied by an application data sheet under 37 CFR 1.76 specifying the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As the applicant, the owner/assignee (if not juristic) can sign replies, RCEs, disclaimers, Fee Transmittals, request status, file an application under 1.46, appoint its own registered practitioner, and grant power to inspect. Compliance with 37 CFR 3.71 and 3.73 is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combining the ownership submission and the action in one paper
rubrics_metrics.description: The action taken by the assignee and the 37 CFR 3.73(b)/(c) submission establishing that the assignee is the appropriate assignee to take such action can be combined in one paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A duplicate copy of the 37 CFR 3.73 statement is not required and should not be submitted (see 37 CFR 1.4(b) and MPEP § 502.04). Once 3.73(b)/(c) is complied with, the assignee may continue to take action without filing a new statement each time provided ownership has not changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing applications — statement required
rubrics_metrics.description: When an assignee files a continuation or divisional application, the application papers must either (A) contain a copy of a statement filed under pre-AIA 37 CFR 3.73(b) (or 37 CFR 3.73(c) for post-AIA) in the parent application, or (B) contain a newly executed statement under 37 CFR 3.73(b)/(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For continuation-in-part applications filed before Sept. 16, 2012 by an assignee, a newly executed pre-AIA 3.73(b) statement must be filed. For design CPAs under 37 CFR 1.53(d), the statement in the parent will serve for the CPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for Continued Examination (RCE) — continuing effect of statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an RCE is filed under 37 CFR 1.114, the application is not abandoned and the statement under pre-AIA 37 CFR 3.73(b) or 37 CFR 3.73(c) in the application will continue to serve as the statement establishing ownership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus no new ownership statement is required solely because an RCE is filed, provided the prior statement remains accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations where ownership must be established (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples where ownership must be established include when the assignee signs a request for status of an application or gives a power to inspect an application; appoints its own registered attorney or agent to prosecute an application; signs a disclaimer under 37 CFR 1.321; consents to filing a reissue application; consents to correction of inventorship; or signs a Fee(s) Transmittal (PTOL-85B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective Sept. 16, 2012, a juristic entity must be represented by a patent practitioner for taking such actions. See cited MPEP sections for each example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations where ownership need not be established (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples where ownership need not be established include when the assignee signs a small entity statement (37 CFR 1.27); signs a statement of common ownership of two inventions; signs a NASA or DOE property rights statement; signs an affidavit under 37 CFR 1.131(a) where the inventor is unavailable; signs a certificate under 37 CFR 1.8; or files a request for reexamination under 37 CFR 1.510.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These specific filings are listed as exceptions to the 37 CFR 3.73 requirement; see the referenced MPEP sections for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post‑Sept.16,2012 juristic-entity signature/representation rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective September 16, 2012, a juristic entity (e.g., organizational assignee) must be represented by a patent practitioner for many papers; juristic entities may sign certain listed papers but other papers submitted on behalf of a juristic entity on or after that date must be signed by a patent practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Juristic entities may sign small entity assertions (37 CFR 1.27), disclaimers (37 CFR 1.321), submissions under 37 CFR 3.73 to establish ownership, powers of attorney (37 CFR 1.32), and powers to inspect (37 CFR 1.14). However, any other paper submitted on behalf of a juristic entity after Sept. 16, 2012 must be signed by a patent practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form usage and duplicate submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PTO/SB/96 may be used to establish ownership under pre-AIA 37 CFR 3.73(b) (or the corresponding post-AIA provisions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A duplicate copy of the 37 CFR 3.73(b)/(c) statement is not required and should not be submitted (see 37 CFR 1.4(b) and MPEP § 502.04). The ownership submission and the action may be combined in one paper.
